> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

Under DP attention, `EngramEmbedding._dp_sharded_lookup` all-gathers every rank's hash ids, looks up the rows each rank owns for all ranks' tokens into a `[DP x tokens, 24, 256]` BF16 buffer, reduce-scatters it, and then `wkv` quantizes the result to MXFP8. The all-gather and the reduce-scatter grow with the DP size and dominate the lookup at decode sizes.

## Modifications

`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_ENGRAM=1` (off by default) replaces that path with two kernels and no collective (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/engram/mega.cuh`), launched by one host call:

- `engram_id_push_kernel`: each rank sends each of its `[T, 24]` hash ids to the rank that owns the row, as 8 B packets `{t * 24 + col, row}` into the owner's receive buffer. The owner is computed from the id, matching `engram.shard_range`: by hash column when `24 % R == 0`, else the equal-row split through an exact multiply-high (the magic and its exactness are checked on the host at load).
- `engram_scatter_kernel`: after a per-block cross-rank barrier (multicast above 2 ranks), each owner reads the requested FP8 rows and E8M0 scales from its own shard (device or per-rank host table) and writes them straight into the requester's wkv input in FlashInfer's 128x4 swizzled layout, so `wkv` takes it as `Mxfp8SwizzledInput` without a separate quantize. Work is dealt as (source, tile) items over a grid coprime with R.
- Both kernels support PDL.

Python: `kernels/ops/communication/mega_engram.py` (`mega_engram_lookup`) and `srt/layers/communication/mega_engram.py` (`MegaEngramWorkspace`, one per process, with one `attach` per Engram table). `Engram.prepare_mega_engram` binds the table after loading when the lookup runs under DP attention on per-rank shards; `Engram.forward` uses it when `wkv` takes 128x4 MXFP8 input and the step's largest DP rank fits `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_ENGRAM_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK` (default: one rank's largest prefill chunk), else it keeps the old path. Every rank takes the same path every step.

Other: `kMaxWorldSize` 16 -> 64 in `sgl_kernel/distributed/communicator.cuh`; `custom_all_reduce_v2._allocate_symmetric_memory` is now public.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP2 (TP2, DP attention 2, EP2, MegaMoE, DSpark, per-rank Engram host tables) on GB300, the switch off and on side by side; sgl-eval 0.1.3 GSM8K, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking with reasoning effort max:

| | Off | On |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K (%) | 97.0 | 97.0 |

Kernel level, both kernels against the current path on GB300 at R = 2, 4 and 8 (8 across two nodes): FP8 bytes, scales and the 128x4 layout are bitwise identical and the `wkv` output is `torch.equal`, for T = 0 to 32768, ragged and idle ranks, both tables alternating, CUDA graph, and back-to-back graphs relying on PDL ordering. The owner computation was also checked offline against `engram.shard_range` for every R from 2 to 64 on the checkpoint's two tables.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

One Engram lookup per layer call on GB300, real-size per-rank host tables, CUDA graph replay, median of 25, slowest rank (us). "Current" includes the id all-gather, the gather, the reduce-scatter and the MXFP8 quantize.

| R | Tokens per rank | Current (us) | This PR (us) | Speedup (x) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 6 | 43.2 | 10.3 | 4.2 |
| 8 | 128 | 85.4 | 19.2 | 4.45 |
| 8 | 512 | 202.2 | 36.1 | 5.6 |
| 4 | 6 | 30.7 | 9.9 | 3.1 |
| 4 | 384 | 96.3 | 30.3 | 3.2 |
| 4 | 4096 | 536.0 | 201.0 | 2.7 |
| 2 | 6 | 29.6 | 12.8 | 2.3 |
| 2 | 1536 | 138.6 | 66.3 | 2.1 |
| 2 | 16384 | 1140.4 | 570.8 | 2.0 |

Not yet measured: end-to-end TPOT, and R >= 16 on GPU.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit (black / ruff on the touched Python files).
- [ ] Unit tests (the kernel was validated with a multi-GPU harness; a registered test is a follow-up).
- [x] Accuracy and speed results above.

+inline constexpr uint32_t kTokenScales = kNumCols * kScaleBytes;  // 192 scale columns per token
+inline constexpr uint32_t kSfTileBytes = 512;
+inline constexpr uint32_t kSfTilesPerRow = kTokenScales / 4;  // 48 column tiles
+
+}  // namespace device::engram::config
+
+}  // namespace sglang

         )
     )

+
+# DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram EP lookup: id push + MXFP8 row push.
+register_kernel(
+    KernelSpec(
+        op="communication.mega_engram_lookup",
+        backend=KernelBackend.JIT,
+        target="sglang.kernels.ops.communication.mega_engram:mega_engram_lookup",
+        capabilities=frozenset({CapabilityRequirement.cuda(min_sm=(9, 0))}),
+    )
+)

@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+"""DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram lookup for EP decode as an id push plus a row push.
+
+``mega_engram_lookup`` sends every hash id of this rank to the rank that owns
+its row, then copies the owned MXFP8 rows (FP8 e4m3 payload, E8M0 scale per 32
+values) straight into the requester's wkv input, with the scales in the 128x4
+swizzled layout the FlashInfer MXFP8 GEMM reads. See
+``csrc/deepseek_v4/engram/mega.cuh`` for the protocol and the buffer-reuse
+invariant (the GEMM that reads ``out`` must run on the same stream before the
+next lookup).
+
+The buffers are views of one symmetric workspace owned by the caller
+(``sglang.srt.layers.communication.mega_engram``).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once, load_jit, make_cpp_args
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
+
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.all_reduce import Communicator
+
+NUM_COLS = 24
+ROW_BYTES = 256
+SCALE_BYTES = 8
+_SCATTER_THREADS = 512
+_UNROLL = 4
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _jit_mega_engram_module(world_size: int) -> Module:
+    if world_size > 64:
+        raise ValueError(f"mega engram supports R <= 64, got R={world_size}")
+    args = make_cpp_args(world_size, _SCATTER_THREADS, _UNROLL)
+    return load_jit(
+        "mega_engram",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["deepseek_v4/engram/mega.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[
+            ("lookup", f"MegaEngram<{args}>::lookup"),
+            ("local_bytes", f"MegaEngram<{args}>::local_bytes"),
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def mega_engram_local_bytes(world_size: int, max_ids: int) -> int:
+    """Bytes of the private, zero-filled buffer ``mega_engram_lookup`` takes as
+    ``local`` for receive slots of ``max_ids`` ids."""
+    return _jit_mega_engram_module(world_size).local_bytes(max_ids)
+
+
+def mega_engram_lookup(
+    comm: Communicator,
+    hash_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_ptr: int,
+    scale_ptr: int,
+    recv: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    sf: torch.Tensor,
+    owner_magic: int,
+    row_start: int,
+    num_rows: int,
+    no_sort: bool,
+    local: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """One Engram lookup: push this rank's ``hash_ids`` ([T, 24] int32,
+    contiguous, T may be 0) to their owners, then serve the rows the peers asked
+    for into their ``out`` / ``sf``.
+
+    ``weight_ptr`` / ``scale_ptr`` address this rank's shard ([rows, 256] fp8
+    and [rows, 8] e8m0, device or registered host memory) whose first global
+    row is ``row_start`` and which holds ``num_rows`` rows. A large shard is
+    read in row order unless ``no_sort`` (set it for device shards).
+    ``recv`` is [R, 1 + max_ids] uint64; ``local`` is this rank's private state
+    (``mega_engram_local_bytes`` uint8, zeroed once). Every rank must call this
+    every step, idle or not.
+    """
+    module = _jit_mega_engram_module(comm.world_size)
+    module.lookup(
+        comm,
+        hash_ids,
+        weight_ptr,
+        scale_ptr,
+        recv,
+        out,
+        sf,
+        owner_magic,
+        row_start,
+        num_rows,
+        no_sort,
+        local,
+    )
+
+
+def get_owner_magic(*, world_size: int, num_rows: int, by_column: bool) -> int:
+    if by_column:
+        return 0
+    magic = -(-(2**64) // num_rows)
+    error = magic * num_rows - 2**64
+    assert world_size * num_rows * error < 2**64, (
+        f"no exact owner magic for {num_rows = }, {world_size = }"
+    )
+    return magic

             total_bytes, device=self.device, group=self.group
         )

@@ -1716,6 +1716,13 @@ class Envs:
     # anonymous mapping per rank holding only its rows, gathered with the
     # all-reduce, and the only layout that gets huge pages without shmem THP.
     SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT = EnvStr("shared")
+    # Engram lookup under DP attention as an id push plus an MXFP8 row push into
+    # wkv's input (kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/engram/mega.cuh), instead of the
+    # all-gather + gather + reduce-scatter. Steps whose largest DP rank has more
+    # tokens than the cap keep the old path; None caps at one rank's largest
+    # prefill (its chunk, else max_prefill_tokens).
+    SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_ENGRAM = EnvBool(False)
+    SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MEGA_ENGRAM_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK = EnvInt(None)
 
     # Kernels and indexer
     SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM = EnvBool(True)

@@ -0,0 +1,212 @@
+"""Symmetric workspace and launch glue of the Engram push lookup (EP decode).
+
+One workspace serves every Engram layer: a receive buffer of id packets per
+source rank, and this rank's wkv input (MXFP8 rows + 128x4 swizzled scales)
+that owners push into. Allocated once for ``max_tokens`` tokens per rank;
+every pointer is fixed, so the two kernels are CUDA-graph capturable.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Optional, Sequence
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+from torch.distributed import ProcessGroup
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.all_reduce import Communicator, PullPlane
+from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.mega_engram import (
+    NUM_COLS,
+    ROW_BYTES,
+    mega_engram_local_bytes,
+    mega_engram_lookup,
+    get_owner_magic,
+)
+
+_ALIGN = 1024
+_SEMAPHORE_BYTES = 128
+_TOKEN_BYTES = NUM_COLS * ROW_BYTES  # 6144 fp8 values per token
+_TOKEN_SCALES = NUM_COLS * 8  # 192 e8m0 scales per token
+
+
+def _align(n: int, a: int = _ALIGN) -> int:
+    return (n + a - 1) // a * a
+
+
+def sf_rows(num_tokens: int) -> int:
+    """Rows of the 128x4 scale layout that hold ``num_tokens`` tokens."""
+    return _align(num_tokens, 128)
+
+
+def _owner_magic(world_size: int, column_bounds: Sequence[int]) -> int:
+    """Owner magic of one table under the per-rank layout: 0 for whole-column
+    shards, else ceil(2^64 / N) with umulhi(x, magic) == x // N for every
+    x < R * N, which holds iff R * N * (magic * N - 2^64) < 2^64. Checks that
+    ``engram.shard_range`` still follows the rule the kernel's owner lookup
+    hard-codes."""
+    from sglang.srt.layers.engram import shard_range
+
+    num_rows = column_bounds[-1]
+    assert len(column_bounds) == NUM_COLS + 1 and 3 <= num_rows < 2**31
+    by_column = NUM_COLS % world_size == 0
+    for r in range(world_size):
+        start, _ = shard_range(num_rows, tuple(column_bounds), r, world_size)
+        expect = (
+            column_bounds[r * (NUM_COLS // world_size)]
+            if by_column
+            else num_rows * r // world_size
+        )
+        assert start == expect, (
+            f"shard {r} starts at {start}, the kernel assumes {expect}"
+        )
+    return get_owner_magic(
+        world_size=world_size,
+        num_rows=num_rows,
+        by_column=by_column,
+    )
+
+
+class MegaEngramWorkspace:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        group: ProcessGroup,
+        device: torch.device,
+        max_tokens: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        """
+        :param group: the TP group (any backend; used for the rendezvous).
+        :param max_tokens: tokens per rank the buffers hold.
+
+        Shared by every Engram layer; each layer binds its table with ``attach``.
+        """
+        from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_v2 import (
+            allocate_symmetric_memory,
+        )
+
+        self.rank = dist.get_rank(group=group)
+        self.world_size = world_size = dist.get_world_size(group=group)
+        self.device = device
+        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
+        # Per rank: [recv | out_fp8 | out_sf | semaphores]
+        self.stride = 1 + max_tokens * NUM_COLS
+        recv_bytes = 8 * world_size * self.stride
+        out_off = _align(recv_bytes)
+        sf_off = _align(out_off + _TOKEN_BYTES * max_tokens)
+        sf_bytes = sf_rows(max_tokens) * _TOKEN_SCALES
+        ws_bytes = _align(sf_off + sf_bytes)
+        # One per scatter CTA; the scatter grid is this count, shrunk until coprime with R.
+        num_sems = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).multi_processor_count
+        total = ws_bytes + _SEMAPHORE_BYTES * num_sems
+
+        self._symm_tensor, symm_mem = allocate_symmetric_memory(total, device, group)
+        slabs = [
+            symm_mem.get_buffer(i, [total], torch.uint8) for i in range(world_size)
+        ]
+        slabs[self.rank].zero_()
+        # Above 2 ranks the scatter barriers signal through multicast.
+        mc_semaphore = None
+        if world_size > 2:
+            assert symm_mem.multicast_ptr, "mega engram needs multicast for R > 2"
+            mc_semaphore = symm_mem.multicast_ptr + ws_bytes
+        self.local = torch.zeros(
+            mega_engram_local_bytes(world_size, self.stride - 1),
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+        dist.barrier(group=group)
+        self.comm = Communicator(
+            pull=PullPlane(
+                self.rank,
+                world_size,
+                workspaces=[s[:ws_bytes] for s in slabs],
+                semaphores=[
+                    s[ws_bytes:].view(num_sems, _SEMAPHORE_BYTES) for s in slabs
+                ],
+                mc_semaphore=mc_semaphore,
+            )
+        )
+        local = slabs[self.rank]
+        self.recv = local[:recv_bytes].view(torch.uint64).view(world_size, self.stride)
+        self.out = local[out_off : out_off + _TOKEN_BYTES * max_tokens].view(
+            max_tokens, _TOKEN_BYTES
+        )
+        self.sf = local[sf_off : sf_off + sf_bytes]
+        dist.barrier(group=group)
+
+    def attach(self, column_bounds: Sequence[int], no_sort: bool) -> MegaEngramTable:
+        """Bind one Engram layer's table: its 25 hash-column boundaries
+        (``EngramConfig.column_bounds``) and whether to never read this rank's
+        shard in row order (``mega_engram_lookup``). Only the per-rank layout: this rank holds ``engram.shard_range``'s
+        rows of the table."""
+        from sglang.srt.layers.engram import shard_range
+
+        bounds = tuple(column_bounds)
+        magic = _owner_magic(self.world_size, bounds)
+        row_start, row_end = shard_range(bounds[-1], bounds, self.rank, self.world_size)
+        return MegaEngramTable(self, magic, row_start, row_end - row_start, no_sort)
+
+
+_WORKSPACE: Optional[MegaEngramWorkspace] = None
+
+
+def get_mega_engram_workspace(
+    group: ProcessGroup,
+    device: torch.device,
+    max_tokens: int,
+) -> MegaEngramWorkspace:
+    """The process-wide workspace; the first call allocates it (collective)."""
+    global _WORKSPACE
+    if _WORKSPACE is None:
+        _WORKSPACE = MegaEngramWorkspace(group, device, max_tokens)
+    assert _WORKSPACE.max_tokens == max_tokens
+    return _WORKSPACE
+
+
+class MegaEngramTable:
+    """One Engram layer's table on a shared ``MegaEngramWorkspace``."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
